text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - Growing KV cache and paged-attention fragmentation detected on production inference pool. Multiple node flaps and rising OOMs. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/inference/alerts/1918451234

julia (oncall): seeing 502/503 spikes for a subset of requests, linked to gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-21. paging metrics show steady kv_cache_pages increase for ~36h.

mike (eng-runtime): copy of latest runtime log snippet:```
2026-03-14T23:12:11Z WARN paged_allocator: slab_fragmentation=0.81 kv_cache_pages=412312
2026-03-14T23:12:12Z ERROR runtime: CUDA error: out of memory at attention_paged.cpp:214
2026-03-14T23:12:12Z ERROR runtime: container restart triggered, oom_count=3
```

sam (eng-sre): tagging this as paging/leak escalation. Is this limited to one model variant or system-wide? any recent rollouts?

julia (oncall): only host models using paged-attn+kv cache so far. No config rollouts in the last 48h. Deploy bot shows no green roll in that window.

elaine (prod-safety): CS reporting 12 active customer tickets for "500 on generation". Severity P2 for now, could go P1 if more nodes drop. Recording customer impact.

mike (eng-runtime): initial hypothesis: slow kv_cache growth combined with slab fragmentation => gradual unusable free memory -> OOMs during attention paging. We saw similar pattern in qa a while back.

julia (oncall): mitigation options - 1) force kv cache eviction on affected pool 2) enable aggressive slab defrag 3) temporarily scale up dedicated nodes to absorb traffic 4) failover route to cheaper non-paged model variant. Any objections?

sam (eng-sre): do 1 + 4 immediately. evict + route is safest low-risk. queuing scale-up while we assess.

mike (eng-runtime): commands I ran:```shell
# evict prefix/kv cache for pool
redwoodctl runtime cache evict --pool=inference-prod-paged --age=1h
# toggle temporary routing to non-paged model variant
redwoodctl routing set --route inference-prod/predict --fallback nonpaged-variant-v2 --priority=high
```
Result: evict returned 124k pages freed. nodes showing drop in kv_cache_pages but fragmentation still high.

julia (oncall): starting the routing change now. will monitor errors and latency.

devinfra-bot: :white_check_mark: routing change applied to 78% of traffic; digests: route-id=rt-4491.

customer-success: heads-up to CS - informing affected customers we're routing them to a non-paged variant temporarily; ask to hold off on sending more tickets until we confirm stabilization.

mike (eng-runtime): follow-up telemetry: evict reduced total pages by 28%, but slab_fragmentation still ~0.75 on some nodes. That means defrag or rolling restarts needed to fully reclaim.

julia (oncall): recommendation: schedule rolling restart for gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-21 during this window. Sam - can you coordinate a drain and restart? prefer sequential to avoid global capacity hit.

sam (eng-sre): starting drain on gpu-node-17:```shell
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l purpose=inference --grace-period=60
```
ETA ~6m to complete evictions. Will restart runtime container after drain.

ops: observed brief latency bump during drain (~120ms p95 to 300ms p95) but 5xxs decreased by ~40% after routing fallback.

devinfra-bot: ALERT - node gpu-node-21 shows repeated cuda memory allocation failures; marking node for manual reboot if fragmentation persists.

mike (eng-runtime): Plan for longer-term: - automatic aged-eviction policy for kv cache - periodic slab defrag job during low traffic - smarter routing to non-paged variants when fragmentation > 0.7 - alert thresholds earlier (kv_cache_pages delta > 50k/12h)

elaine (prod-safety): can we get a customer impact summary and timeline for comms? CS will want a short explanation + ETA to full restore.

julia (oncall): quick customer summary for CS: "We detected gradual KV cache growth in the paged-attention allocator that caused fragmentation and intermittent CUDA OOMs on a subset of GPU nodes. We routed affected traffic to a non-paged variant, evicted aged KV pages, and are doing sequential node restarts. Expected full restore in 1-2 hours; engineers continuing root cause analysis."

customer-success: ack, sending update to affected customers now.

sam (eng-sre): gpu-node-17 restart complete. runtime came back healthy; slab_fragmentation dropped to 0.48 on that host. Starting drain on gpu-node-21 next.

julia (oncall): switching to 1hr monitoring cadence. I'll own the incident until handoff in 4h. Mike, please capture heap profiles and attach to the postmortem. Sam, add restart timeline and routing changes to incident timeline.

mike (eng-runtime): collecting profiles:```shell
redwoodctl runtime dump-heap --node=gpu-node-21 --out=/tmp/heap-g21.tgz
scp /tmp/heap-g21.tgz eng-runtime@analyzer:/data/
```
Will upload to incident ticket 1918451234-incident.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT NOTES - mitigation applied: evict+fallback routing+sequential restarts. Monitoring continues. Postmortem owner: mike (eng-runtime). Handoff owner until next oncall: julia.

julia (oncall): thanks team. if we see any new OOMs re-escalate immediately. filing live timeline now.

ops: closing loop - 5xx counts down to baseline, p95 latency trending down. Keeping this in watch for 2h. :thumbsup:
